tagline: four services on the same port: **S3** (68/107 Smithy ops, real bucket-policy / ACL / PAB enforcement), **DynamoDB** (18 ops, full UpdateExpression, queryable GSI/LSI, batch + atomic transactions, 573-word reserved-word enforcement), **SQS** (23 ops including FIFO + Queue Policy enforcement), **SNS** (19 ops including AddPermission/RemovePermission + FilterPolicy evaluation + Topic Policy enforcement). Cross-service wiring: S3 → SQS event notifications, S3 → SNS → SQS multi-hop fan-out. All services verified against Python + JS + AWS CLI v2 conformance suites. Opt-in via `--services s3,dynamodb,sqs,sns`. Pre-`v1.0.0`; minor breaking changes are expected

wedge.behaviour: Presigned URL with a custom header — request sent *without* it → clean `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch`
`Accept-Ranges: bytes` on every GetObject / HeadObject response
Conditional-header split (GET/HEAD: all four; PUT: `If-Match`/`If-None-Match` only; CopyObject: `x-amz-copy-source-if-*`)
wedge.localstack: Inconsistent — some headers accepted but not enforced

wedge.behaviour: Multipart ETag = `md5(concat(binary-MD5-of-each-part)) + "-" + N`; `EntityTooSmall` when any non-final part < 5 MiB

divergences.title: Bucket-policy-style `Condition` blocks are skipped
divergences.body: in IAM policies (same caveat as S3 M14). Not applicable to DynamoDB resource policies since we don't model IAM at all.

divergences.title: Imports/Exports
divergences.body: — out of scope for v0.2.x. Returned as `ValidationException` (unknown target) for now. Candidate for a future patch if there's demand.

divergences.title: Global Tables, DAX
divergences.body: — out of scope indefinitely. Global Tables is meaningless on a single-region emulator; DAX is a separate cache service with its own binary protocol, wrong shape for an emulator.

divergences.title: Parallel scan (`TotalSegments > 1`)
divergences.body: will return `ValidationException`.

divergences.title: GSI auto-fetch-from-base-table
divergences.body: for non-projected attrs is a client-SDK behavior; nanostack returns only the projected attrs.

divergences.title: Streams: single open shard per stream
divergences.body: (no shard splitting / closed-shard semantics). Sequence numbers are a monotonic per-stream counter rendered as 21-digit zero-padded decimals. Re-enabling a stream rotates the shard ID (matches AWS's "label changes on re-enable").

divergences.title: Streams: 24h retention is approximate
divergences.body: — records older than 24h are dropped on next consult, but a write-heavy stream may evict records younger than 24h once the 1000-record bound is hit.

divergences.title: TTL: sweep interval defaults to 5 seconds
divergences.body: (vs AWS "best-effort within 48h"). Tunable via `--ttl-sweep-interval-seconds N` (range 1..=3600). 5s is right for local-dev tests; production-faithful retry-after-eviction-delay simulations would set this higher.

divergences.title: TTL: status transitions snap immediately
divergences.body: AWS shows ENABLING / DISABLING transients for ~1h after each call; we move straight to ENABLED / DISABLED. Tests asserting on transient states won't match.

divergences.title: PartiQL grammar
divergences.body: : Phase 1 covers what AWS supports — SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE with WHERE constrained to PK eq + optional SK predicate (eq / lt / le / gt / ge / BETWEEN / begins_with). FilterExpression-style scan filters (OR / NOT / IN / AND-of-non-key-attrs) and richer SET (list_append, if_not_exists) land in future patches. Quoted identifiers are case-sensitive; unquoted identifiers case-fold to lowercase, matching AWS.

divergences.title: PartiQL `LIMIT` in statement
divergences.body: : rejected — AWS doesn't support it either. Use the request-level `Limit` parameter instead.

divergences.title: PITR target time is ignored
divergences.body: `RestoreTableToPointInTime` accepts `RestoreDateTime` / `UseLatestRestorableTime` but always snapshots the current source state. Documented divergence — same as LocalStack. Real time-travel would require a write-ahead log we don't keep.

divergences.title: `EarliestRestorableDateTime` is synthetic
divergences.body: = `max(table_created, now - 35d)` even when PITR is disabled. boto3 reads the field unconditionally so we return a plausible value.

divergences.title: Backup snapshots aren't encrypted
divergences.body: AWS uses KMS; we don't model KMS at all.

divergences.title: `BackupSizeBytes` is an estimate
divergences.body: = sum of item-file sizes after JSON serialization.

divergences.title: JSON wire only
divergences.body: boto3 v1.34+, JS SDK v3, and CLI v2 all use the JSON wire by default. The legacy query-string / XML form is **out of scope** — users on older SDKs should upgrade.

divergences.title: FIFO high-throughput mode deferred
divergences.body: `DeduplicationScope=messageGroup` and `FifoThroughputLimit=perMessageGroupId` (the per-group-throughput accounting mode AWS added for high-volume FIFO workloads) are not modelled — attributes accepted & round-tripped but the accounting isn't built. v0.3.x patch if a user asks.

divergences.title: FIFO SequenceNumber width
divergences.body: : 20-digit zero-padded decimal (u128). AWS docs say "up to 39 digits". Strict-width parsers may need to relax.

divergences.title: Long polling = in-handler sleep loop
divergences.body: ReceiveMessage with `WaitTimeSeconds > 0` blocks the handler thread, polling the queue every 100ms until a message arrives or the deadline expires. AWS-real uses a server-side event loop; we don't. Wastes one handler thread per long-poll; acceptable for local dev.

divergences.title: No connection-cancellation detection on long polling
divergences.body: A client that drops mid-poll keeps the handler sleeping until the deadline. AWS-real would notice and return immediately.

divergences.title: No rate limits
divergences.body: AWS enforces per-account caps on queues + sends/sec. We accept everything.

divergences.title: No encryption at rest
divergences.body: (no SSE-SQS, no SSE-KMS). Same divergence as DDB backups.

divergences.title: Cross-account principals not supported
divergences.body: SigV4 in nanostack verifies only against the configured `--access-key`; a request signed with a different account's key fails verification before reaching policy evaluation. Anonymous (`Principal: "*"`) grants work end-to-end via raw unsigned requests; explicit cross-account `Principal: { AWS: "arn:aws:iam::<other-account>:root" }` grants don't have a way to be exercised in nanostack.

divergences.title: `AddPermission` only constructs Allow statements
divergences.body: (AWS-real shares this constraint). Users who need Deny statements must install a hand-built Policy via `SetQueueAttributes`.

divergences.title: Policy `Condition` blocks are skipped
divergences.body: (statement evaluates as `no_match`, same caveat as the S3 evaluator). Inherited from `auth/policy_eval.zig`.

divergences.title: `MessageMoveTask` runs synchronously
divergences.body: Real AWS executes tasks asynchronously with `MaxNumberOfMessagesPerSecond` throttling and exposes intermediate `RUNNING` status. We drain on Start, never expose `RUNNING`. `MaxNumberOfMessagesPerSecond` accepted but ignored. Move tasks are in-memory only — not persisted across restart.

divergences.title: MessageMoveTask cancellation is a count read
divergences.body: Because tasks complete synchronously on Start, `CancelMessageMoveTask` always returns the final moved count rather than cutting a running task short.

divergences.title: Query wire protocol only
divergences.body: No JSON migration to track; modern AWS SDKs (boto3, aws-sdk-js v3, AWS CLI v2) all use query.

divergences.title: FIFO topics deferred
divergences.body: `.fifo` suffix rejected. Future v0.4.x patch.

divergences.title: Internal cross-service dispatch bypasses the authz hook
divergences.body: `s3/events.zig` calls `snsPublish` at the storage layer (S3 → SNS notifications), and the SNS handler dispatches `sqsSendMessage` directly for fan-out — neither path reaches the SNS authz hook. Same documented divergence as v0.3.4 S3 → SQS dispatch. AWS uses a service-principal model we don't surface.

divergences.title: Topic-policy Condition blocks unsupported
divergences.body: `auth/policy_eval.zig` skips Condition blocks (treats them as no-match), the same constraint that applies to S3 bucket policies and SQS queue policies. A statement with a Condition block evaluates as `no_match` and contributes nothing to the decision.

divergences.title: Filter-policy operators deferred
divergences.body: v0.4.1 evaluates exact string-array shapes (e.g. `{"category": ["news", "sports"]}`); operator objects (`prefix`, `anything-but`, `numeric`, `exists`, `cidr`, `suffix`) are treated as no-match (the subscription is filtered out). AND across top-level keys, OR within a rule array. Future v0.4.x patch will land the operator set.

divergences.title: Only `sqs` protocol fires
divergences.body: `lambda` / `http` / `https` / `email` / `email-json` / `sms` subscriptions are stored but never deliver.

divergences.title: `ConfirmSubscription` auto-confirms
divergences.body: SQS subs at Subscribe time; for non-SQS protocols, the confirmation is a no-op that flips the persisted bit (since those subs never fire anyway).

divergences.title: Signature fields are stubs
divergences.body: `Signature` is the literal `"nanostack-stub"`; `SigningCertURL` is `https://nanostack.local/cert.pem`. nanostack doesn't do KMS-style signing. Matches LocalStack.

divergences.title: MessageAttributes only on envelope path
divergences.body: When `RawMessageDelivery=true`, MessageAttributes are not propagated to the SQS message's MessageAttributes field. AWS does this; we don't (yet).

divergences.title: Cross-account principals out of scope
divergences.body: Same SigV4 limitation as the rest of nanostack — only the configured `--access-key` validates.

flows.notes: PutObject / CopyObject / CompleteMultipartUpload → `s3:ObjectCreated:*`; DeleteObject / DeleteObjects → `s3:ObjectRemoved:Delete` or `:DeleteMarkerCreated`. Filter rules (prefix + suffix). Wildcard event matchers (`s3:ObjectCreated:*`, `s3:*`).
TopicConfiguration entries now fire to SNS topics. The Message field of the SNS publish carries the S3 event envelope verbatim.
One Publish → every SQS subscriber receives the SNS envelope (or raw Message bytes with RawMessageDelivery=true).
Combines the above. The SQS subscriber sees an SNS envelope whose `Message` field is the S3 event envelope.
CloudFunctionConfiguration is parsed + stored, never fires. Lambda service not implemented (planned v0.5.0).
DDB Streams emit to their own `GetRecords` API (v0.2.2). Cross-service piping deferred.

timeline.name: SQS robustness
timeline.scope: Cold-start message rehydration; MessageRetentionPeriod sweeper; 6 unrouted ops (AddPermission/RemovePermission/ListDeadLetterSourceQueues/MessageMoveTask trio).
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. Closes SUPPORT.md ↔ behaviour drift; lands all unrouted ops. Queue Policy enforcement deferred to v0.3.3.
timeline.headline: Patch release: SQS robustness

timeline.name: Queue Policy enforcement
timeline.scope: Wire policy_eval.zig into a new src/services/sqs/authz.zig hook; SQS action map; thread Principal through the SQS service context.
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. Last SQS gap closed. After this, SQS is feature-complete + fully enforced.
timeline.headline: Patch release: SQS Queue Policy enforcement

timeline.name: S3 → SQS event notifications
timeline.scope: Wire PutBucketNotificationConfiguration QueueConfiguration entries to actually fire on PutObject / DeleteObject / Copy / CompleteMultipartUpload, with prefix/suffix filter eval and AWS-format event envelope.
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. The strategic unlock — first cross-service wiring proven. Canonical local-dev serverless workflow (upload → queue → worker) works end-to-end.
timeline.headline: Patch release: S3 → SQS event notifications. The strategic unlock

timeline.name: SNS
timeline.scope: 17 ops (topic CRUD + subscriptions + Publish/PublishBatch + tags). SNS → SQS fan-out + S3 → SNS dispatch. Query+XML wire protocol layer added.
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. First minor since v0.3.0 SQS. Multi-hop S3 → SNS → SQS works end-to-end.
timeline.headline: Minor release: SNS joins S3 + DynamoDB + SQS

timeline.name: SNS robustness
timeline.scope: Tags persistence across restart; AddPermission / RemovePermission (Policy mutation, accept-store-roundtrip); per-entry MessageAttributes on PublishBatch; FilterPolicy evaluated at publish time (exact string-array shapes).
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. Closes the four divergences flagged in v0.4.0's SUPPORT.md. Topic Policy enforcement deferred to v0.4.2 (same v0.3.2 → v0.3.3 SQS trajectory).
timeline.headline: Patch release: SNS robustness

timeline.name: SNS Topic Policy enforcement
timeline.scope: Wire policy_eval.zig into a new src/services/sns/authz.zig hook; SNS action map; thread Principal through the SNS service context.
timeline.rationale: Shipped 2026-05-18. Mirrors v0.3.3 SQS verbatim. After this, SNS is feature-complete + enforced modulo FIFO.
timeline.headline: Patch release: SNS Topic Policy enforcement

timeline.name: Lambda
timeline.scope: Function CRUD + Invoke + S3 / SQS / DDB-Streams event-source mappings. Likely a sidecar-process execution model (we don't host an in-Zig runtime).
timeline.rationale: The big multi-service hop. Highest payoff for the v1.0 claim. (Minor.)

timeline.name: Polish + multi-profile + bench
timeline.scope: Multi-profile state isolation (deferred from v1 per §17a); end-to-end performance pass against the broader surface; documented "production local-dev surface".
timeline.rationale: "Curated multi-service surface workflow-ready." Stabilization, not new features. (Major.)
